program_name: Global Law and Transnational Legal Studies
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). The entire 3-year, 180-ECTS degree is delivered in English; it is a single UNITO degree, not an English pathway inside an Italian-named programme and not an interuniversity/joint degree. Official UNITO/AlmaLaurea records list the delivery mode as 'convenzionale - blended' (conventional with blended components) from the 2023 cohort onward, but the language of instruction remains English. Note: the Italian official title of the same degree is 'Global law and transnational legal studies - diritto della globalizzazione e studi giuridici transnazionali'; this is only the bilingual registry name, not a bilingual curriculum.
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy - Department of Law (Dipartimento di Giurisprudenza), University of Turin
degree_class: L-14 (Scienze dei servizi giuridici / Legal Services Sciences). UNITO internal programme code: 0707L32 (the earlier cohort code for the same degree was 0707L31). Ministerial 'codicione': 0010106201400008. Course catalogue ID: 12344.
admission_type: Open access / free admission (corso ad accesso libero - no restricted number of places), but enrolment is conditional on sitting the TARM (Test for the Assessment of Minimum Requirements), which for a.y. 2026/2027 is delivered through the CISIA TOLC-SU. A non-passing English score does not block enrolment; it triggers an OFA (additional learning obligation). Separate quotas exist for international applicants: 250 places reserved for non-EU citizens residing abroad and 25 places reserved for Marco Polo programme students. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy: enrolment follows the standard UNITO open-access enrolment procedure - register for and sit a TOLC-SU (or a valid English TOLC-E taken between 1 January 2025 and 30 November 2025), then matriculate within the UNITO enrolment windows. Applicants in this group holding a FOREIGN qualification must instead apply through Apply@UniTo: second admission call 19 February - 15 April 2026; third admission call 1 July - 14 September 2026 (restricted-number programmes only, therefore not applicable to this open-access degree); fifth admission call for open-access undergraduate programmes 25 August - 19 October 2026. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU citizens residing abroad (visa applicants): apply through Apply@UniTo in the second admission call, 19 February - 15 April 2026, and then submit the pre-enrolment (visa) application on the Universitaly platform by 15 July 2026 for a.y. 2026/2027. A first admission call (typically opening in the autumn preceding the academic year) could not be verified for the 2026/2027 cycle because apply.unito.it and en.unito.it returned 403 (Cloudflare) to direct fetching. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: TARM (Test for the Assessment of Minimum Requirements), administered as a CISIA TOLC. For a.y. 2026/2027 the valid test for this programme is the TOLC-SU (Humanities TOLC). The TOLC-SU can be taken on paper (at a venue) or online (TOLC@CASA) and may be repeated. Exemption: candidates who already took the ENGLISH TOLC-E between 1 January 2025 and 30 November 2025 are not required to also take the TOLC-SU. There is no separate written entrance exam, interview, motivation letter or portfolio: the TOLC result is not selective for admission (the programme is open access) - it only determines whether an OFA is assigned. [uncertain]
academic_requirements: 1) Upper-secondary school diploma (Italian 'diploma di scuola secondaria superiore') or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad and recognised as valid for university access, plus any further requirements set out in the programme's educational regulations (regolamento didattico). 2) A satisfactory level of general knowledge, good expressive ability and aptitude for reasoning and argumentation, verified via the TOLC-SU. 3) Mastery of English at CEFR B2 or above (see language_requirements). 4) No minimum GPA / grade threshold and no numerus clausus: the programme is open access with no restricted number of places for the general pool. 5) Reserved international quotas: 250 places for non-EU citizens residing abroad and 25 places for Marco Polo students. 6) Applicants with a foreign qualification must have their qualification verified by the UNITO International Students Office (Declaration of Value / CIMEA statement of verification or comparability may be requested) and must complete all administrative steps within the UNITO deadlines. 7) OFA (Obbligo Formativo Aggiuntivo): an insufficient score in the English/reading-comprehension part of the TOLC does not prevent enrolment but creates an additional learning obligation that must be cleared during the first year of enrolment. [uncertain]
language_requirements: English: CEFR B2 level is the stated requirement ('the student must possess mastery of the English language with a level of knowledge at least at the B2 level of the CEFR'). Verification is carried out through the TOLC rather than by mandatory submission of an external certificate: the mandatory English ('Inglese') section of the TOLC-SU is used, and scoring below the threshold (reported as fewer than 16 points in the English section, corresponding to fewer than 5 points in the Reading Comprehension sub-section) still permits enrolment but assigns an English OFA to be completed within the first year. Candidates who took the ENGLISH TOLC-E in the qualifying window (1 January 2025 - 30 November 2025) are exempted from the TOLC-SU. Italian: no Italian language certificate is required for this programme, because the UNITO rule requiring a B2 Italian certificate for non-EU visa applicants applies only to programmes taught in Italian; this degree is taught entirely in English. Whether a recognised external English certificate (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge) can be substituted for the TOLC English section could not be confirmed on an official page. [uncertain]
required_documents: Via Apply@UniTo (apply.unito.it), for applicants with a foreign qualification: 1) Valid passport (mandatory for non-EU citizens) or identity document; 2) Upper-secondary school final diploma / school-leaving qualification; 3) Academic transcript of the final years of secondary school with subjects and grades; 4) Where applicable, evidence that the qualification gives access to higher education in the issuing country (e.g. Declaration of Value, CIMEA Statement of Verification / Statement of Comparability, or a diploma supplement) - the International Students Office verifies authenticity and applicants are advised to provide proof of authenticity already at application stage; 5) Certified translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish if the documents are not issued in one of those four languages (documents in Italian, English, French or Spanish are accepted as they are); 6) TOLC-SU (or qualifying English TOLC-E) attendance/score record from the CISIA account; 7) Any further documents requested after submission (the University may ask for additional documentation both after application and at enrolment); 8) At enrolment: residence permit or visa documentation for non-EU applicants, and payment of the first instalment (regional tax for the right to university study plus stamp duty). Incomplete applications are rejected. The application call on Apply@UniTo is split by citizenship/residence status - applying in a call you are not eligible for means the application will not be considered. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes:
SOURCE ACCESS LIMITATION: none of the official pages could be fetched directly during this research. www.globallaw.unito.it refused TLS connections (ECONNREFUSED on 130.186.3.24:443) to both the WebFetch client and curl, and the browser tool denied navigation to that host; apply.unito.it and en.unito.it returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare bot protection); unito.coursecatalogue.cineca.it returned HTTP 405. All content above was therefore reconstructed from search-engine indexed extracts of those same official unito.it pages (globallaw.unito.it admission_requirements.html, tarm.html, how_to_apply.html, key_information.html; en.unito.it programme and international-student pages; apply.unito.it news pages) rather than from a first-hand page read. Every field is consequently marked uncertain and should be re-verified against the live pages before publication.

SPECIFIC OPEN POINTS:
1) Programme scope: this IS a full standalone English-taught degree (not a pathway/curriculum inside an Italian degree, not an interuniversity/joint degree). This part is well corroborated across UNITO, AlmaLaurea and the CINECA catalogue.
2) Programme code inconsistency: official UNITO pages currently label the degree [0707L32], while the Department of Law course browser and the 2023 CINECA catalogue entry still use [0707L31] for earlier cohorts. Same degree, different cohort codes.
3) English threshold wording conflict: one official extract states the OFA is triggered below 16 points in the 'English' section of the TOLC-SU, another states below 5 points in the 'Reading Comprehension' (Comprensione del testo) section. These are likely two different sub-scores of the same test, but the exact rule needs confirmation on the live TARM page.
4) Whether an external English certificate (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge) can replace or waive the TOLC English section could not be confirmed on any official page.
5) Admission-call dates: the second call (19 Feb - 15 Apr 2026) and fifth call (25 Aug - 19 Oct 2026) come from apply.unito.it's 'When can I apply?' news page as indexed. A FIRST admission call (normally the autumn window aimed at non-EU citizens residing abroad) is referenced by the numbering but its 2026/2027 dates were not recoverable; en.unito.it itself notes that 2026/2027 information 'is being updated' and may change. Treat all dates as provisional.
6) The globallaw.unito.it 'How to apply' page carries a note that the Apply@UniTo call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy, and the programme's own application portal page currently reads 'Application closed'. This appears to refer to a specific closed call rather than to the programme's overall availability to non-EU applicants (the programme has 250 reserved non-EU places), but the interaction between the programme-level call and the university-level Apply@UniTo calls is not fully clear and should be checked directly.
7) Tuition: no programme-specific fee page exists; UNITO applies a university-wide scheme. For 2026/2027 the ISEE Parificato is being replaced for international students by a scale based on the GDP per capita (PPP) of the country of residence, with reported full-comprehensive contributions of EUR 300/500/700/1,000 per year plus a first instalment of about EUR 156 (regional study tax + stamp duty); third-party sites quote a maximum around EUR 2,800/year for the standard scheme. These figures were not verified on an official 2026/2027 page.
8) Required documents list is assembled from UNITO's general international-applicant documentation pages, not from a programme-specific document checklist; a programme-specific checklist may exist on the Apply@UniTo course page (course id 543).
9) Per task scope, no polito.it sources were used.
